claim: The Eiffel Tower is located in Paris.
reason: The evidence states that the Eiffel Tower is a lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France.

claim: Mount Everest is the highest mountain on Earth above sea level.
reason: The evidence explicitly states that Mount Everest 'is the highest mountain on Earth above sea level.'

claim: Marie Curie won Nobel Prizes in both physics and chemistry.
reason: The evidence states that she shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel. It also states that she won the 1911 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

claim: The Amazon River flows into the Atlantic Ocean.
reason: The evidence explicitly states the Amazon discharges into the Atlantic Ocean, notes that its mouth is at the Atlantic with Belém as the major port, and says the Amazon basin drains west to east across Brazil to the Atlantic.

claim: Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the Moon.
reason: The evidence states that Armstrong, as commander of the 1969 Apollo 11 mission, 'became the first person to walk on the Moon.' It also describes him as the first to step onto the lunar surface, with Aldrin following about 19 minutes later as the second human to walk on the Moon.

claim: The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci.
reason: The evidence opens by describing the Mona Lisa as a half-length portrait painting by the Italian artist Leonardo da Vinci. It also says the attribution has never been seriously questioned.

claim: Canberra is the capital city of Australia.
reason: The evidence opens by stating that Canberra is the capital city of Australia. It also says Canberra was established to serve as the seat of government for the new nation.

claim: The Pacific Ocean is the largest of Earth's oceans.
reason: The evidence states the Pacific Ocean is 'the largest and deepest of Earth's five oceanic divisions' and 'the largest division of the World Ocean,' which directly supports the claim.

claim: The Python programming language was created by Guido van Rossum.
reason: The evidence states that Python was conceived by Guido van Rossum in the late 1980s at CWI. It also says he began implementation in December 1989, first released it in 1991, and is called 'Python creator Guido van Rossum.'

claim: The Berlin Wall fell in 1989.
reason: The evidence states that the Wall stood from 1961 to 1989 and that the evening of 9 November 1989 is known as the night the Wall came down. Its opening on that date is referred to as 'the fall of the Berlin Wall.'

claim: The Eiffel Tower is in Berlin.
reason: The evidence states the Eiffel Tower is a lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. This directly contradicts the claim that it is in Berlin.

claim: Mount Kilimanjaro is located in Peru.
reason: The evidence states that Mount Kilimanjaro is a large dormant stratovolcano in Tanzania and the highest mountain in Africa. This contradicts the claim that it is located in Peru.

claim: Albert Einstein was born in France.
reason: The evidence says Einstein was born in Ulm, in the Kingdom of Württemberg in the German Empire, on 14 March 1879, and calls him 'German-born'. This contradicts the claim that he was born in France.

claim: The Moon is larger than the Earth.
reason: The evidence gives the Moon's diameter as 3,474 km, roughly one-quarter of Earth's, and its mass as 1.2% (about 1/81) of Earth's. This directly contradicts the claim that the Moon is larger than the Earth.

claim: Pride and Prejudice was written by William Shakespeare.
reason: The evidence states that Pride and Prejudice is a novel by English author Jane Austen, not William Shakespeare. This directly contradicts the claim.

claim: Tokyo is the capital of China.
reason: The evidence states Tokyo is the capital and most populous city of Japan, not China; it also lists Beijing as a separate capital name example, contradicting the claim.

claim: The Titanic sank in the Pacific Ocean.
reason: The evidence states that Titanic's lifeboats were lowered into the North Atlantic and that the wreck lies in Titanic Canyon off the coast of Newfoundland, which places the sinking in the Atlantic Ocean, not the Pacific.

claim: Jupiter is the smallest planet in the Solar System.
reason: The evidence states Jupiter is 'the largest in the Solar System' and 'the largest planet in the Solar System,' which directly contradicts the claim that it is the smallest.

claim: The Berlin Wall fell in 1979.
reason: The evidence states that the Wall stood from 1961 to 1989, and that the night of 9 November 1989 is known as the night the Wall came down. This contradicts the claim that it fell in 1979.

claim: Penicillin was discovered by Isaac Newton.
reason: The evidence states that penicillin was discovered in 1928 by the Scottish physician Alexander Fleming, not Isaac Newton.

claim: Gustave Eiffel's favorite food was onion soup.
reason: The evidence covers Eiffel's life, career, works and death, but it never mentions his food preferences, so it neither confirms nor contradicts the claim that his favorite food was onion soup.

claim: Marie Curie kept a pet cat named Radium.
reason: The evidence covers Marie Curie's life, career, discoveries, honours, and death in detail, but it never mentions any pet, let alone a cat named Radium. It neither confirms nor contradicts the claim.

claim: Neil Armstrong owned a red bicycle as a child.
reason: The evidence describes Armstrong's childhood, including his early interest in flying, building model aircraft, and his first airplane ride. It never mentions a bicycle, red or otherwise, so the claim can be neither confirmed nor contradicted.

claim: Leonardo da Vinci's favorite color was green.
reason: The evidence does not mention Leonardo da Vinci's favorite color. The only reference to colours concerns the robes Bernardo Baroncelli was wearing when he died, which says nothing about Leonardo's preferences.

claim: Guido van Rossum has a pet dog named Monty.
reason: The evidence mentions his wife, Kim Knapp, and their son, and says Python was named after Monty Python's Flying Circus. It never mentions any pet dog, let alone one named Monty, so the claim can be neither confirmed nor contradicted.

claim: In 2019, Canberra received more tourists on Tuesdays than on any other weekday.
reason: The evidence provides no information about tourist visitation patterns by day of the week in 2019 or any other year, so the claim can be neither confirmed nor contradicted.

claim: Albert Einstein's favorite breakfast was porridge.
reason: The evidence covers Einstein's diet only in terms of his sympathy for vegetarianism and his later meat-free eating. It never mentions his breakfast preferences or porridge, so it neither supports nor contradicts the claim.

claim: Jupiter's Great Red Spot will disappear completely by the year 2100.
reason: The evidence states that mathematical models suggest the Great Red Spot is stable and will be a permanent feature of the planet. This contradicts the claim that it will disappear by 2100, even though the evidence also notes the storm has been shrinking.

claim: Jørn Utzon kept a personal diary written entirely in French.
reason: The evidence lists Utzon's written works, including logbooks and journal articles in English and Danish, but it never mentions a personal diary or any writing in French. Nothing in the text confirms or contradicts the claim.

claim: The original frame of the Mona Lisa was carved by a left-handed craftsman.
reason: The evidence says only that the Mona Lisa was removed from its original frame at some point and that its current frame was given by Comtesse de Béhague in 1909. It never says who made the original frame or whether that craftsman was left-handed.
